fields.label: Page title
segments: Buying your first home: a step-by-step guide

fields.label: Body
segments:
Buying your first home is a big step. This guide walks you through it, from your first budget to the closing table.

1. Know your budget. Add up your monthly income and your debts. Lenders look at your debt-to-income ratio: the share of your monthly income that goes to debt payments.

2. Get prequalified. Prequalification with ClearPath takes about 10 minutes and uses a soft credit inquiry, so it does not affect your credit score. You get an estimate of how much you can borrow.

3. Save for the down payment and closing costs. Some loan programs accept a smaller down payment, but a smaller down payment usually means private mortgage insurance (PMI) and a higher monthly cost.

4. Compare loan types. A fixed-rate mortgage keeps the same rate for the whole term. An adjustable-rate mortgage (ARM) starts with a fixed rate that can change later. Our 30-year fixed rate is from 6.375% APR for well-qualified borrowers.

5. Make an offer and close. After the seller accepts your offer, we order the appraisal, finish underwriting and schedule your closing.

Talk to a ClearPath mortgage loan officer: clearpathcu.example/mortgage

ClearPath Credit Union NMLS #401822. Equal Housing Opportunity. Federally insured by NCUA.

fields.text: Get prequalified for a ClearPath mortgage

fields.label: Body
fields.text:
Know your budget before you start house hunting.

Prequalify for a ClearPath mortgage in about 10 minutes. We use a soft credit inquiry, so prequalifying does not affect your credit score. You get an estimate of how much you can borrow and which loan types fit you: fixed-rate, adjustable-rate, and loans for first-time buyers.

Prequalification is not a loan approval or a commitment to lend. Your final loan terms depend on a full application, an appraisal and underwriting.

Start your prequalification: clearpathcu.example/mortgage/prequalify

Equal Housing Opportunity. Federally insured by NCUA.

findings.explanation: is a trigger term. The content must also include disclosure D-7 "Personal loan APR range and term". If an ad for closed-end credit states a trigger term (the amount or percentage of a down payment, the number of payments or period of repayment, the amount of any payment, or the amount of any finance charge), it must also state the down payment, the terms of repayment, and the annual percentage rate. If the rate can increase after the loan is made, the ad must say so.
